data.title: kadence assumptions map
body: # kadence assumptions map
- **Subject:** the decision to build kadence as an append-only tracker with sprints, after the competitive analysis showed the category is taken
- **Product type:** new → the full model of 8 categories
- **Method:** Torres (Value / Usability / Viability / Feasibility) + Ethics / GTM / Strategy / Team; ranked by `Risk = Impact × (1 − Confidence)`
## Main finding

> **Updated 2026-09-02 after [Probe A](DOC-55).** Assumption #1 was partly tested on 8,396 merge commits from 130 repositories: conflicts in tasks happen in 15.4% of repositories — not refuted, but not confirmed either. Confidence raised from low to medium, risk 8.0 → 5.0. The remaining assumptions stay untested.
**We thoroughly tested the easiest thing and tested nothing that matters.**

Both assumptions with high confidence are technical (`feasibility`), and those are exactly the ones backed by the spike's measurements. All eight of the riskiest are about **value and going to market**, and none of them has anything behind it but the author's reasoning.
| Quadrant | Count |
| Investigate | 1 |
| Proceed | 1 |
| Defer | 2 |
The technical spike was the right step and gave honest numbers — but it answered the question "can we build this", while all the real risks stand in the question "does anyone need this".
## Registry
| # | Assumption | Category | Conf. | Impact | Risk | Quadrant |
| 1 | Conflicts when merging tasks are a pain teams feel in practice | Value | **medium** ⬆ | 10 | **5.0** ⬇ | [Probe A](DOC-55) done: 15.4% — ambiguous, next Probe B |
| 2 | Sprints and velocity are needed by a git-native audience | Value | low | 9 | **7.2** | Test Now |
| 3 | Developers will move off free GitHub Issues | GTM | low | 9 | **7.2** | Test Now |
| 4 | An agent needs file access, not MCP | Value | low | 8 | 6.4 | Test Now |
| 5 | We will gather an audience against git-bug and Backlog.md | GTM | low | 8 | 6.4 | Test Now |
| 6 | Time-travel is valuable every day, not only in a demo | Value | low | 8 | 6.4 | Test Now |
| 7 | A CLI without a TUI is enough for the first users to stay | Usability | low | 7 | 5.6 | Test Now |
| 8 | The window of opportunity is 12–18 months | Strategy | low | 7 | 5.6 | Test Now |
| 9 | Migration from Backlog.md is a real acquisition channel | GTM | low | 6 | 4.8 | Investigate |
| 10 | A solo developer will carry the MVP to closing the gap | Team | medium | 8 | 4.0 | Test Now |
| 11 | OSS without monetisation will outlive the author's enthusiasm | Viability | medium | 7 | 3.5 | Test Now |
| 12 | The journal will not become an instrument of surveillance | Ethics | medium | 6 | 3.0 | Defer |
| 13 | Append-only eliminates conflicts | Feasibility | **high** | 10 | 2.0 | **Proceed** |
| 14 | 200 ms is achievable on real repositories | Feasibility | high | 6 | 1.2 | Defer |
## Devil's advocate

**The PM objects.** The biggest risk is not that conflicts hurt nobody — it is that they hurt **rarely**. A task is moved by one person, not by three at once. Our spike modelled three because that is the worst case; in reality it may be once a month. A tool that brilliantly solves a rare problem loses to a tool that tolerably solves a daily one.

**The designer objects.** We plan to ship v0.1a without a TUI against competitors who have a TUI and a web board. The first user will compare not architectures but what they see. "They have a kanban, you have a list in a terminal" — and no argument about append-only will be heard.

**The engineer objects.** We chose an event log because it elegantly solves conflicts, and we measured that it works. But we never checked whether anyone complained about conflicts in Backlog.md. Their task `task-4.12` is their internal backlog, not a user report. We may have built a measured answer to an unmeasured question.
## Three tests that change the decision

1. **#1 — conflicts.** Ask not "do conflicts hurt" (everyone will say yes) but "tell me about the last time this happened". No concrete case in three months — the assumption is false, and the product's main thesis goes with it.
2. **#2 — sprints.** Ask how they measure velocity now. If they do not and it bothers nobody, the second differentiator falls too, and what remains is technical elegance with no buyer.

3. **#7 — the TUI.** Cheap and fast: show a CLI mock-up to five developers and see whether they are willing to try it without a board at all. The answer directly determines whether v0.1a has the right to ship without a TUI.
## What this changes in the existing documents
- **PRD, section 4.2** — rewrite: the category is taken, the competitors are different ones.

- **PRD, section 11** — the recommended next step was "a spike, then 5 interviews". The spike is done, and the map confirms: interviews are now not the next step but the **only meaningful** step before code.
- **SPEC.md** — remains valid. It describes *how* to build, and these assumptions do not affect it; it is simply waiting on the decision whether to build.
